Name: 5P
Notes: Has the same frame data and a near-identical hitbox to 2P.
Launches balls somewhat slowly at a horizontal angle.
Description: Great at checking low airdashes and for anti-airing after running under an opponent. Sends balls quite far despite its speed which is excellent for pre-emptively beating jumping.

Name: 5K
Notes: Jump and dash cancellable.
Launches balls somewhat slowly at a horizontal angle.
Description:
Superb poke that serves as a compliment to Venom's more committal S normals. The high active frames and low recovery make it very effective at stuffing the opponent's buttons and approaches. With good timing, it can even meaty while staying safe against wakeup reversals.
The angle it sends, in conjunction with its jump and dash cancels, make 5K a key tool for ball manipulation both in neutral and on oki.

Name: c.S
Notes: Jump and dash cancellable.
Launches balls somewhat slowly at a moderate upwards angle.
Description:
Go-to pressure normal without a ball set, and can be used flexibly if you do have one, due to its wide gatling options.
Very important in combos as, alongside f.S and 2S, it combos to 2H naturally on grounded opponents, as well as exclusively into 6H, and is also easy to use after a 5K dash cancel or special moves in the corner.

Name: f.S
Notes: Launches balls somewhat quickly at a horizontal angle.
Description: A very long-range poke that is quite safe when spaced, especially when combined with special cancels like Stinger Aim or QV, allowing Venom to create space and harass opponents easily. In return, its reward is minimal, as it has too much range for any of its gatlings to combo consistently at its best range. Even with a counterhit, the best you can get is a partially charged QV for a hard knockdown and a ball set, though that's plenty for Venom.

Name: 5H
Notes: Launches balls quickly at a horizontal angle.
Tumbles on air hit into a soft knockdown.
Description:
Fairly stubby, and not especially safe or rewarding. Fast enough to be gapless from S normals, unlike 6H or 2H, so it is useful to create space in blockstrings if Venom is in a bad position. The hitbox extends far back enough to hit balls set inside or slightly behind Venom, a place none of his other moves cover.
While its short range makes it intimidating to use as a counterpoke, its hitbox is fully disjointed and it has a lot of active frames, so it has its place, even if it should be used more sparingly. It sees a lot more use in combos, especially in the corner, due to its long tumble allowing for unique extensions such as a fully charged QV. Most useful application is when used within the gap of Dark Angels pop and Robo-Ky's explosion, it will launch opponents full screen and break the wall.

Name: 5D
Notes: Causes floating crumple on ground hit.
Launches opponent on air hit.

Launches balls somewhat quickly at a somewhat slight upwards angle. The move can still hit balls even after active frames, due to Venom spinning his pool cue by his feet during recovery; in this case, it will be safe on block or even lead to a combo on hit depending on positioning. This can occur if Venom is directly on top or slightly in front of a P ball set.
Description:
Universal overhead attack. Tapping gives a fast but weak overhead, while holding down will give a much slower but much more powerful strike.
Fairly standard dust. Can lead to meterless combos with a well placed ball.
On-hit, holding will activate for a large combo opportunity.

Name: 2P
Notes: Has the same frame data and a near-identical hitbox to 5P.
Launches balls slowly at a horizontal angle.
Description:
Obligatory 5f mash, but stands out due to having massive range for a light normal. Confirms into itself, 6P, or the H version of very consistently.
The massive reach of this normal makes it an abnormally good punishing tool as well as a fantastic low startup, low recovery poke against short ranged characters.

Name: 2K
Notes: Launches balls somewhat slowly at a very slight upwards angle.
Description: A very important button for Venom, forming the low half of his high/low mixup and being a solid 2K in its own right with respectable range and speed. It combos into 2D even at its max range, starting Venom's powerful ball okizeme.

Name: 2S
Notes: Launches balls somewhat quickly at a horizontal angle.
Description: Similar to f.S, trading a tiny bit of startup speed and range for a bigger disjoint, a longer active frames, and the ability to hit low profile moves. It recovers exactly as fast as f.S, so which one is the best to use varies depending on the situation, though 2S is a safer bet at most ranges.

Name: 2H
Notes: First hit launches balls somewhat quickly at a relatively steep downwards angle, spiking the ball back upwards. Second hit launches balls somewhat quickly at a relatively steep upwards angle.
Description:
This move is almost exclusively combo filler. It can be used in blockstrings as a frame trapping low with delay, but can be awkward when blocked by an opponent as 2nd hit will not connect vs FD. It is very punishable on block, so it must be cancelled into a special to be safe.
The second hit launches, allowing for stable confirms into charged QV midscreen and Carcass Raid both midscreen or in the corner, making 2H a combo staple.

Name: 2D
Notes: Hard knockdown on ground hit or Counter Hit.
The first hit vacuums the opponent and keeps them standing.
Launches balls at a steep upwards angle.
Description:
Famously annoying normal. Its excellent range allows it to cancel from 2K easily, granting a hard knockdown and access to Venom's setplay. Just like 2H, its two hits also give it a lot of flexibility, with the choice to either cancel the vacuuming first hit to when within range for a short combo or letting the second play out and cancelling it into a ball set. In pressure, it allows an easy way to vacuum opponents into 's range. While it is inferior to 6K in this regard, 2D being a crouching normal makes inputting both charge moves less challenging.
2D's most notable trait is its low profile, which in conjunction with its high active frames makes it great for blowing up various pokes; for example, it goes right under Ky's f.S. Compared to 6P, it doesn't go under as many things, but can be significantly more rewarding if it scores the hit.

Name: 6P
Notes: Launches on hit, hard knockdown on Counter Hit.
Launches balls somewhat slowly at a mild upwards angle.
Description: Universal anti-air with a great hitbox. Use it to crush mid pokes and reliably anti-air your opponent's jump-ins. Due to the angle it launches the opponent when airblocked, it's harder to maintain pressure after it than something like c.S, 5K or even a rising air normal, though you can set a ball or two and get your zoning going regardless.

Name: 6K
Notes: Launches balls backwards somewhat quickly at a horizontal angle. Handy as a side switch during Tryambaka.
Hitting an opponent with this move with a ball right behind Venom will reduce Venom's Hitstop without the ball connecting, making the Move +5 on block and +8 on standing hit.
Description: Vacuums on hit and block. If the opponent fails to use Faultless Defense it creates looping plus frames with H Carcass Raid. On hit, can combo into the latter for a modest pickup midscreen, and a wallbreak in the corner. The recovery is fairly low, allowing other pressure resets or reversal baits.

Name: 6H
Notes: Combos from 2P/5P on CH on standing opponents, and from CH 2K/5K on crouchers.
Launches balls quickly at a sharp downwards angle, spiking the ball back upwards.
After using Ball Set (Multiple), can be used to hit all four balls at once.
Description:
Venom's highest damage normal and ideal combo ender for its hard knockdown, while also having use as a frametrap after c.S thanks to its high reward. The huge hitbox gives it some utility in neutral as well; having a ball on screen makes it considerably better for this purpose since it means Venom will be able to cancel safely from it even on whiff, amending its long recovery, though the range it covers cannot be understated.
Keep in mind that it doesn't reach its max range on its first active frame, which can cause some combos to drop if you don't account for it, but apart from that, 6H is great for opening the door to Venom's most powerful okizeme and is the easiest way to set up Ball Set (Multiple).

Name: j.P
Notes: Launches balls somewhat slowly at a horizontal angle.
Has the same frame data as 5P and 2P.
Description: Good air-to-air since it's lightning fast and has long range, but not very rewarding.

Name: j.K
Notes: Air jump and air dash cancellable.
Launches balls somewhat slowly at a horizontal angle.
Description: Huge hitbox and slightly upwards angle make this an excellent rising anti-air. Occasional combo filler when used with an airdash cancel for extra corner carry.

Name: j.S
Notes: Air jump and air dash cancellable.
Launches balls quickly at a sharp downwards angle, spiking the ball back upwards if it has enough time to bounce off the ground.
Description: Venom's general purpose air normal, featuring good range, a cross-up hitbox, and hitting decently far below Venom. Its low attack level makes it hard to use from an instant airdash unless it's cancelled into something or Faultless Defense Cancel (FDC) is used. Very useful in ball mixups, since it will hit balls downwards along your own jump arc, making them easy to follow up after.

Name: j.H
Notes: Jump and air dash cancelable.
Launches balls quickly at a sharp downwards angle, spiking the ball back upwards.
Description:
Venom's main jump-in option as it has the most frame advantage from his jump-ins. Even though this is his main jump-in, this move will need to be delayed on IAD to get more plus frames. The alternative is making use of the low frame advantage to threaten j.D or land to make an opponent hesitant to retaliate. IAD j.S > j.H will not be possible unless you superjump first.
On air hit it spikes into a soft knockdown, not particularly useful besides for preventing from wallbreaking.

Name: j.D
Notes: Fully safe or even plus on block without FD, jails into H Carcass Raid without FD.
Air jump and air dash cancelable.
Launches balls quickly at a somewhat sharp downwards angle, spiking the ball back upwards.
Description:
A sharply angled, special cancelable divekick where each hit must be blocked high. Has very high reward on hit and requires specific counterplay to punish.
Generally Venom will try to land it if he has a knockdown or by gatling into it from a jump-in. Since it's a long, multi-hitting attack, Venom can easily use the time he spends during j.D to store charge and confirm if he's being pushed out by FD. He can cancel into or delayed up close and or a jump cancel when farther away.

Name: Ground Throw
Notes: Can throw the opponent either forward or backwards.
Hard knockdown on hit.
Counter Hit state during recovery.
Description:
Universal throw that sets up a variety of safe oki options. Often preferable to because of its speed and ease of use.
Midscreen, a simple auto-timed safejump is possible via backdash > IAD j.H. Alternatively, a meaty ball can be setup with S or an H into an immediate 5K dash cancel. Both options are reversal safe when executed properly, but the latter leaves Venom much closer to his opponent.
In the corner, a dash cancelled OTG c.S leaves more than enough time for a 5K safejab. Cancelling the OTG into H gives you a reversal safe meaty ball.
You can maintain advantage using after a throw, but you don't have the time to get the sorts of mixups which are possible off 2D and 6H.

Name: Air Throw
Notes: Can throw the opponent either forward or backwards.
Hard knockdown on hit.
Counter Hit state during recovery until landing.
Description: A good anti-air in a pinch that launches the opponent fullscreen away for Venom to begin his zoning. If throwing the opponent into the corner, Venom will be bounced back a short distance, making it difficult to get follow-up pressure. Use the knockdown to set balls instead.

Name: Ball Set
Notes: Balls can be interrupted and hit while they are drifting to their assigned location, meaning Venom can hit balls at points otherwise impossible.
Each ball spawn spends a different amount of time drifting after spawning.
Hitting balls has a fixed 5f of hitstop.
Description:
Spawns a pool ball that then drifts to its corresponding position according to the used button, inert balls will remain for about 4 seconds before despawning. Which ball to spawn in any given scenario varies wildly and is one of the most essential parts of playing Venom effectively. This isn't his only way to set a ball and cannot create enhanced balls unlike charged , but it is the fastest and safest way.
Attacks that hit a ball behave the same way as if they made contact with the opponent. For example, if hitting a ball with 5K, it can be cancelled normally, such as into a jump or a dash; hitting a ball with f.S will allow Venom to cancel into 5H, 2H or a special move, and so on. This is an essential technique for Venom's advanced okizeme setups, as well as creating more complex zoning patterns.

Name: Ball Set (Multiple)
Description: Places every ball from Ball Set at once. Unlike Ball Set, the balls spawn at their assigned locations immediately rather than drifting to them from Venom's hand.

Name: Ball Hit
Notes: Ball patterns are integral to understanding how to maximize Venom and diagrams on the ball patterns can be found here.
Description: Venom's iconic way of controlling neutral and applying pressure to the opponent. Venom can hit the ball with various normals and specials which cause them to move in a certain direction. When hit by a normal the path the ball will take will be the same, but for specials the path it takes can vary by a variety of factors (speed, angle, P1 vs P2, opponent position, etc). Often will be used to protect venom as he moves forward or try and force opponent to take action.

Name: QV
Notes: The attack is identical for each attack button; the only difference is where the summoned ball moves to when it comes out.

Uncharged version is a soft knockdown, while partial and fully charged cause a hard knockdown. The fully charged version also launches much higher on hit, allowing for a follow-up juggle in most cases.
Cannot be released before the startup of the next charge level. For example, if you charge beyond the uncharged version, then the move will never come out any sooner than frame 28.
Description:
Venom creates a dark orb a distance away from him which bursts and creates a ball. The balls that spawn will drift to the same position as their equivalent versions from Ball Set. The move has a deadzone immediately in front of Venom. Used with pokes, creates distance on block with surprisingly high reward on hit which makes it a good frametrap tool.
The button can be held to charge the move which will improve the hitbox, damage and strength of the launch as well as creating an upgraded ball with full charge. Partial charge is a very common combo ender for Venom since it gives a hard knockdown.

Name: Stinger Aim
Notes: Can be charged, improving travel speed and damage. The charged version enhances the projectile in the same way as charged QV, bouncing the ball back towards Venom and keeping it on screen to be launched again later.
The projectile and the cue strike are separate hits; the strike nullifies projectiles and will launch other balls in front of Venom quickly along with its own.
H version's ball goes a little over 1 stage worth of distance. Meaning the ball will always bounce off the wall even if venom's back is in the corner.

The ball spawns on frame 6 for the H version, and frame 7 for the S version. If Roman Cancelled during startup, unless struck beforehand, the ball will be deleted if Venom tries to use his charge attacks or air Carcass Raid.
Description:
A strike with the cue that launches a ball straight ahead and deletes projectiles. S launches at a moderate speed. H starts up faster and launches balls faster but is considerably more punishable.
It's best used for long-range play and to interact with inert balls or ones spawned by . Balls that are near Venom will be hit by the cue strike which gives them a straightforward trajectory. Hitting a ball with the ball will perform a split shot, charging the attack makes the ball fly faster and uses an upgraded ball which rebounds towards Venom on hit.
H is extremely fast which makes it good for beating other characters with fullscreen options and to confirm from light starters. It shouldn't be used at close range unless trying to goad an opponent into a surprise attack from delayed PRC.

Name: Carcass Raid
Notes: Can be charged, improving travel speed and damage, as well as creating a more durable ball.
The ball spawns on frame 6 for both versions. If Roman Cancelled during startup, unless struck beforehand, the ball will be deleted if Venom tries to use his charge attacks or air Carcass Raid.
Description:
A complementary special to Stinger Aim where Venom ricochets a ball off the ground towards the air. The S version has a more diagonal trajectory and longer recovery; its main use is to control the air above and in front of Venom, as well as hitting balls at trickier angles.
The H version, on the other hand, is Venom's most essential combo tool; its quick speed and slight launch allows it to be used as a launcher and combo extender from all kinds of moves, most notably letting him convert into a full combo from his 2K/j.D mix. The move's fast startup and wealth of plus frames let him loop pressure resets repeatedly at close range which forces opponents to use to keep him out.
H Carcass Raid's short horizontal range can be circumvented by ing it from a dash cancellable normal, most commonly c.S, allowing for otherwise impossible combo extensions and suffocating blockstrings.
H Carcass Raid can be used as an alternative method of setting balls that makes them ascend rather than descend after spawning, while spawning low enough to hit 6P.

Name: Carcass Raid (mid-air)
Notes: Can be charged, improving travel speed and damage, as well as creating a more durable ball. Venom hangs in the air while the move is charging, delaying his landing.

The ball spawns on frame 4 for the S version, and frame 5 for the H version. If Roman Cancelled during startup, unless struck beforehand, the ball will be deleted if Venom tries to use his charge attacks or air Carcass Raid.

If Venom lands during the move's startup, the ball will not be launched and recovery changes. Data shown in ( ). The ball instead be placed low to the ground without a hitbox, similar to using Ball Set.
Description:
Carcass Raid, but in the air! The balls follow a slightly different trajectory from the grounded version; Air Carcass Raid is mainly useful for stalling Venom's descent and poking the opponent with a bit more safety from a jump. Should not be overused however, as it has a lot of landing recovery.
Landing and creating a ball has a strange side-effect on the ball, wherein it is deleted if Venom tries to use his charge attacks or Air Carcass Raid again. This property is fixed if it is struck with a normal, but that issue limits its potential as a setplay method considerably.

Name: Tryambaka
Notes: 1 Damage: 5P, 2P, j.P
6 Damage: Ball Hit, 6P, 5K, 2K, 6K, c.S, f.S, 2S, 2D, j.K, j.S, j.D, QV (623X), Carcass Raid H ([2]8H), Air Carcass Raid (j.236S/H)
13 Damage: 5H, 2H, 6H, j.H, 5D, 5[D], Stinger Aim ([4]6S/H),
27 Damage: Stinger Aim Held ([4]6[S/H])
Description:
A command grab that turns the victim into a ball. A ball-ified player can be hit identically to the rest of Venom's balls and collides with other balls on screen when in motion. The ball state expires quickly (though it is extended slightly for each hit) which will leave the victim comboable afterwards.
While certainly unorthodox, Tryambaka has potent setup and wall-breaking potential; since the opponent floats around at Venom's mercy, its corner carry is immense when capitalized on, allowing Venom to corner the opponent easily and set up his scariest okizeme. Plus, it's just plain fun to use.
While the opponent is in the ball state, the base damage of each of Venom's moves is extremely reduced. However, damage dealt during this state also ignores the opposing character's damage received modifier and Guts, and RISC damage scaling does not occur.

Name: Dark Angel
Notes: Performs 23 hits on block.
Description:
Venom creates a huge, dark ball that slowly travels forwards and changes its properties depending on whether it hits or is blocked. On hit, it deals a few hits, launching the opponent upwards after which Robo-Ky will shoot them with a tracking missle which explodes after making contact with the opponent or the ground. On block, it persists for a long time, hitting over and over and locking the opponent down for a potential mixup opportunity. A strong point of this super is it cannot be bursted or YRC'd until the end of the super as the ball will still be out and catch the recovery of those moves.
As Venom is completely free to act after he recovers, this move shines in mixups and combos where its flexibility allows for all sorts of shenanigans. Note that the Robo-Ky finisher will occur as long as the opponent gets hit once by the ball, which can catch an opponent offguard. This applies to OTG hits from the initial projectile as well, which can be used to force an opponent to block Robo-Ky on wakeup for even more mixups. Note that the Robo-Ky finisher will not occur if he is still busy from a recent grab.

Name: Navaratna Runout
Notes: Both the move itself and any Pool balls on screen will vacuum the opponent on hit.
Each vacuumed Pool ball deals 10 base damage on contact with the opponent.

The move will vacuum in Pool balls during the entirety of its active frames, and stays active after being PRC'd. This allows you to send even more Pool balls into the vortex for the cost of a full tension gauge!

Each Pool ball absorbed increases the damage of the final hit by 5 and increases its minimum scaling factor as follows - 0 Balls - 20% Minimum Scaling 1 Ball - 25% Minimum Scaling 2 Balls - 30% Minimum Scaling 3 Balls - 35% Minimum Scaling 4+ Balls - 40% Minimum Scaling
Description:
Venom creates a pocket in front of him that hits multiple times, finishing in a large explosion. If any balls are on-screen when this move is used (including the opponent if they were turned into a ball by ), they are sucked into it to improve its damage, making this super a powerful combo ender under the right conditions.
Despite being an overdrive, it can be a functional counterpoke due to the massive disjointed range and safety on-block. If Venom gets hit after the screen freeze then the projectile remains, potentially letting him combo afterwards.
